x: Rendering and state The Python component serializes spaday properties. A browser custom element passes those values to Pierre’s imperative FileDiff renderer. This adapter does not recreate a diff viewer in Python or imitate its output with static HTML. The custom-elements manifest defines Python properties, enum choices, and events. Generated bindings use spaday’s normal actions and bindings. Integration code stays in this peer package; no core spaday changes are required. Updates and lifecycle Property changes are batched within a microtask. The adapter retains the same upstream viewer between updates, allowing Pierre to maintain its DOM and scroll state. Programmatic selections use the upstream non-notifying API, preventing selection events from feeding back into the server. Disconnecting cleans up the upstream instance. The example hosts a Pydantic model in transports. Browser actions call Python endpoints; transports publishes changes back to spaday bindings. A background Python task updates the proposed file independently. The Pyodide preview runs that same Python module in a browser worker. Its endpoint bridge and transports frames stay inside the browser. It does not substitute a separate JavaScript demo for the Python application.

The wheel contains the browser entry point and lazy syntax/theme chunks. Those chunks are served alongside the component, without external syntax-asset requests. The Pyodide preview downloads its Python runtime and dependencies separately. Annotations accept plain text, not arbitrary HTML. Editing, merge-conflict resolution, custom JavaScript render callbacks, SSR, and worker-pool configuration are outside this initial wrapper.

How-to guides Display a patch Pass unified patch text to Diff(patch=patch_text). For multi-file or multi-commit patches, patch_file=0 selects the first file; subsequent indices follow patch order. Create one Diff per index to display several files. A non-null patch takes precedence over old_file and new_file. Bind patch to null to return to file comparison. Invalid patches or indices produce a visible error and a render-error event. Partial patches contain only their supplied context. Use complete old/new files when users need to expand omitted lines. Synchronize selection Bind the selected range to a transports-hosted model and send user changes to an endpoint: from spaday import CallEndpoint, event_value from spaday_diffs import Diff comparison = ( Diff(old_file=before, new_file=after) .bind("selected_lines", "selected_lines") .on( "selection-change", CallEndpoint("POST", "/api/review/selection", event_value()), ) ) The endpoint receives {"range": {"start": 2, "end": 4, "side": "additions"}}. Store that range in the hosted model. Set it to null to clear selection. Programmatic selection updates do not emit another event. See spaday_diffs/example.py for the model, endpoint, WebSoc

comparison = Diff( old_file=before, new_file=after, annotations=[ {"side": "additions", "line": 3, "text": "Check this value."}, ], ) Lines are one-based. Line 0 adds a file-level note. Annotation text is rendered literally, not interpreted as HTML.

comparison.css( spa_diffs_surface="#101827", spa_diffs_text="#e2e8f0", spa_diffs_added="#68d391", spa_diffs_deleted="#fc8181", ) Set theme_type="dark" for dark syntax highlighting. Package tokens inherit from spaday shell tokens; direct overrides apply only to that viewer. Use theme to choose another Shiki syntax theme.

Reference Diff is an alias for generated SpadayDiff. Both render <spaday-diff>. package registers the diffs component package, CSS, JavaScript, and served upstream version. Properties Property Description old_file Original {name, contents, lang?} file. Null represents an added file. new_file Updated {name, contents, lang?} file. Null represents a deleted file. patch Unified patch text. When non-null, takes precedence over old_file and new_file. patch_file Zero-based file index across all commits in a patch. Defaults to 0. selected_lines Selection {start, end, side?, endSide?}, using one-based lines and additions/deletions sides; null clears. Programmatic writes do not emit selection-change. annotations Plain-text annotations [{side, line, text}], using one-based lines or 0 for a file-level note. diff_style Diff layout; split by default. theme Shiki theme name or {light, dark} theme names. Defaults to Pierre’s themes. theme_type Color mode; system by default. overflow Code overflow; scroll by default. line_numbers Show line numbers; true by default. header Show the filename header; true by default. indicators Change markers; bars by default. line_diff Inline highlighting granularity

Event Detail selection-change {range: {start, end, side?, endSide?}}, or {range: null} line-click {line, side} render-error {message} Line numbers are one-based. Sides are "additions" or "deletions". Events bubble across shadow boundaries. Only user selection changes emit selection-change.

TOKENS maps Python css() keyword names to spaday Token objects. Keyword Controls Shell fallback spa_diffs_surface viewer background --spa-surface spa_diffs_text default text and filenames --spa-text spa_diffs_muted line numbers --spa-muted spa_diffs_added added lines --spa-success spa_diffs_deleted deleted lines --spa-danger spa_diffs_accent selection and modified files --spa-accent spa_diffs_font_size code font size None spa_diffs_line_height code line height None CSS spellings use hyphens, for example --spa-diffs-surface. Tokens control viewer chrome and diff colors; syntax colors come from the selected Shiki theme.

Python 3.11+, spaday 0.12+, and a modern browser with CSS light-dark() support. The wheel includes Pierre Diffs 1.5.2 and its browser assets. The example additionally uses transports, Pydantic, Starlette, and Uvicorn.

Compare two files Install the package: pip install "spaday-diffs[examples]" Create a Python file containing: import uvicorn from spaday.backends.starlette import serve from spaday_diffs import Diff, package before = {"name": "settings.py", "contents": "retries = 1\n"} after = {"name": "settings.py", "contents": "retries = 3\n"} comparison = Diff(old_file=before, new_file=after, diff_style="split") app = serve(comparison, packages=[package]) uvicorn.run(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=8000) Run the file. Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. The deleted value appears on the left and the added value on the right. Change diff_style to "unified" and run it again. Both versions now appear in one column. The component definition is unchanged when used with spaday’s notebook backend. For a working reactive application, run python -m spaday_diffs.example after installing spaday-diffs[examples]. Select a line number. The status beneath the comparison reports the selection received by Python.

Open the browser example or jump to the component gallery. The browser runs the packaged Python example in Pyodide. Buttons and selections call Python handlers, then transports sends updated model state back to spaday. The gallery renders real Diff components.

pip install "spaday-diffs[examples]" python -m spaday_diffs.example Open http://127.0.0.1:8017. The proposed file updates every ten seconds; line-number selections round-trip to Python. From a checkout, use make develop, make build, and make test. Build the standalone browser preview with make pyodide-example, then serve dist/lite over HTTP. make test-pyodide-example exercises it in Chromium.
